The preserved-copy behaviour works, with an honest caveat: **actually capturing and storing pages is build-time integration** — in the prototype the "View copy" opens a *simulated* snapshot and the Internet Archive link is illustrative. What you're confirming here is the behaviour and where it lives.

Open the two versions. In **each**:

1. On a bookmark, find the **🗂 Saved copy · captured … · View copy** line and click **View copy** — you get a preserved snapshot page (clearly marked as a saved copy, not the live page).
2. Look at the **"Deep Learning" PDF** bookmark — its copy is labelled **(PDF)** and opens the PDF itself, as you asked.
3. From **More ▾**, choose **Save to Internet Archive** — an **Internet Archive** link is added alongside the saved copy.

The difference is **when the copy is made**:

- **Option A — automatic:** http://maker:4001/preserve-a.html
  Every bookmark you save gets a preserved copy automatically (try saving a new link — it arrives already copied). One item is intentionally left without a copy so you can see the manual **Save a copy** action too.

- **Option B — on demand:** http://maker:4001/preserve-b.html
  Nothing is copied until you choose **Save a copy** on a bookmark. Internet Archive is always a separate, explicit choice.

Assumptions to confirm: the preserved copy is meant to **survive the original changing or disappearing**; a **PDF's copy is the PDF file**; and **Internet Archive is always an explicit, separate action** (not automatic).

**Which should be the default — automatic copies for every save (A) or on-demand (B)? And do the preserved-copy and Internet Archive behaviours match your intent?** (If A, I'd expect automatic copying to be something you can switch off in Settings — tell me if you'd want that.)
